reader_question: Where do the fights over removals, spending and watchdogs stand?
grade_line: Checked by the atlas, record by record: its issue records, as of October 15, 2026
title: Of six disputes over checks on power, the Supreme Court had decided one by October 15, 2026, and had acted by interim order in three others.
measure_line: The status of six issues in the atlas on checks on power, each as its record stood when the atlas checked it on October 15, 2026, United States
notes: Each chip is our reading of the atlas’s status text, and the words under it give the case or finding and its date. An interim order holds while its case continues. The third interim order the title counts came in Issue I068, the dispute over withheld appropriations, on September 26, 2025, in Department of State v. AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition; that issue’s chip gives its latest event, a watchdog finding.
Statuses may have changed since October 15, 2026.
alt: Six issues with status chips. Decided: Issue I163, at-will removal of regulators, by Trump v. Slaughter on June 29, 2026. Interim order: Issue X06, the attempted removal of a Federal Reserve governor, and Issue X05, domestic troop deployments. In court: Issue I070, the firing of inspectors general. Watchdog finding: Issue I068, withheld appropriations. Counted: Issue X18, nationwide injunctions.

table.caption: Status of six issues on checks on power, as of October 15, 2026

chart_notes: Every status chip takes one style, and its word gives the status. Each issue’s ID sits in its own chip before its title.

I163.words: Trump v. Slaughter, June 29, 2026: the Supreme Court ruled 6 to 3 that the President may remove Federal Trade Commission members at will.

X06.words: Trump v. Cook, June 29, 2026: the Supreme Court, 5 to 4, refused to let the removal of Governor Lisa Cook take effect while her case continues.

X05.words: Trump v. Illinois, December 23, 2025: on its emergency docket, the Supreme Court left in place an order blocking the deployment of federalized National Guard troops in Illinois.

I070.words: Storch v. Hegseth: the latest docket entry listed, a July 20, 2026 minute order, shows no ruling on the merits.

I068.words: The Government Accountability Office found two more violations of the Impoundment Control Act on October 7, 2026.

X18.words: The Congressional Research Service (report R49022, July 7, 2026) counted 50 cases with nationwide injunctions against the administration from its first day, January 20, 2025, to June 27, 2026, 16 of them after Trump v. CASA, decided June 27, 2025.

notes_internal: Maker A, round 2. Data plan row 79, rule 14.89. Domain D05 and Illinois (X05) from the sidecar.

Data lead rulings (d) and (e): grade line 'Checked by the atlas, record by record'; one chip style for every status, no red; typed ID chips (Rule 13.9). Chip words are our reading of V7's status text; each status's words quote V7's case and date.

Every figure checked by script (maker A's tools/figs.py, scratch, round 2): each status's case, vote and date in V7's status text (Slaughter 6 to 3 and Cook 5 to 4 on June 29, 2026; Illinois December 23, 2025; the July 20, 2026 minute order; GAO October 7, 2026; 34, 16 and 50 cases around June 27, 2025); every record checked October 15, 2026.

Second run, data lead MA-5: the title names the six disputes as checks on power, the atlas's group for all six, and counts three interim orders: X06 and X05, and I068's emergency application of September 26, 2025, in V7's text; I068's chip stays Watchdog finding, its latest event.

Second run, data lead's H09 ruling on X18: the window stays as the Congressional Research Service gives it, the administration's first day to June 27, 2026, with that reason in the chip's words; 50 (34 plus 16) and report R49022 of July 7, 2026 checked against V7's status text by script.
